subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native trust metadata and enforcement contract should OpenClaw use for durable memory ingestion, storage, retrieval, review, and expiration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines security semantics, persisted state shape, plugin/API visibility, config policy, and upgrade behavior that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, migration behavior, retrieval policy, and plugin exposure before code lands.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance MVP
options.body: Use #42647 and #48519 as prerequisites for durable provenance, then add memory-specific trust tiers and policy enforcement once source lineage is settled.

options.title: Defer To External Integrations
options.body: Document external MCP or plugin memory systems as optional solutions and intentionally leave default OpenClaw memory without native trust enforcement for now.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, migration behavior, retrieval policy, and plugin exposure before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current routing signal from prior #7707 review context and recent memory host/plugin boundary work.
